changes.change: Exchange Web Services (EWS) retirement update
changes.before: As previously announced, EWS will be retired in favor of Microsoft Graph , which offers improved security, modern authentication, and broader capability support.
changes.says: We're updating the timeline and process for the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online.

changes.change: Cross-tenant Calendar Sharing on Cross-Tenant Access slips to 15 October, two weeks after EWS starts switching off on 1 October
changes.before: Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.
changes.says: Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026 .
changes.why: From 1 October partner organisations can stop seeing shared calendars from your tenant, and the Cross-Tenant Access replacement for calendar sharing is not due until 15 October. The control that governs this cross-tenant data flow is also moving from the Exchange admin to the identity admin.

changes.change: EWS retirement and EWSAllowedAppIDs enforcement
changes.says: Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online will begin retirement on October 1, 2026 , with full retirement beginning April 1, 2027 .

changes.change: EWS starts requiring a configured EWSAllowedAppIDs list, and Microsoft will generate one from 60 days of observed usage where none exists
changes.says: As part of the final phase of Exchange Web Services (EWS) retirement, Microsoft is updating how the EWSAllowedAppIDs setting is applied in Exchange Online .

changes.change: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips and calendar sharing move onto Cross-Tenant Access policy
changes.why: The control moves from the Exchange admin's organisation relationships to the identity admin's Cross-Tenant Access policy. Anyone who tuned outbound data sharing in Exchange should check whether their CTA policy says the same thing — because after the move, CTA is what is enforced.

changes.change: Hybrid tenants with on-premises mailboxes and online archives, and tenants sharing free/busy with on-premises orgs, must keep EWS on
changes.why: The EWS shutdown that starts today is also an attack-surface reduction; this post is Microsoft telling some tenants to keep EWS enabled, so the exception must be scoped to one app ID rather than left open.

changes.change: EWS needs an EWSAllowedAppIDs allow list from 10 October; EWSEnabled=True alone stops being enough
changes.before: Microsoft will auto-populate allow lists for some tenants, but organizations must review, maintain, and migrate from EWS to Mi… [What and why] As previously communicated in MC1466860 and MC1447678 , Microsoft is continuing the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS) in Exchange Online.
changes.says: Starting October 10, 2026, Exchange Online tenants must configure EWSAllowedAppIDs to allow Exchange Web Services (EWS) access; EWSEnabled=True alone will no longer suffice.
changes.why: The list Microsoft generates is built from 60 days of traffic, so the quarterly job, the archive tool and the IR script that reads mailboxes over EWS are exactly what it misses. After 10 October the allow list is also the complete inventory of applications that can still reach mailboxes over EWS, which makes it a control worth owning rather than inheriting.

changes.change: Update Teams devices to a minimum app version ahead of the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS)
changes.says: Update Microsoft Teams Rooms on Android, phones, and panels to the minimum app version released in February 2026 before October 2026 to avoid losing calendar functionality due to the retirement of Exchange Web Services (EWS).

todo.text: Run Get-OrganizationRelationship and Get-SharingPolicy in Exchange Online PowerShell as Microsoft's post shows; where calendar sharing with another Microsoft 365 tenant is in use, warn the business owners about the two-week gap and plan the Cross-Tenant Access policy for it now.
Compare the existing Exchange organisation relationships against the outbound settings in Cross-Tenant Access policy and reconcile the two before Microsoft does it for you.

If you have on-premises mailboxes with online archives or org relationships with on-premises partners, confirm EWSEnabled is TRUE and that EWSAllowedAppIDs lists only the dedicated hybrid app; do not remove the on-premises servers' EWS permissions yet.

Before 10 October run Get-OrganizationConfig -RetrieveEwsOperationAccessPolicy | Format-List EwsAllowedAppIDs, compare it with the EWS usage report, add every AppID the business still needs in one write (the list is replaced, not appended), and record who approved each entry.

changes.change: My Sign-Ins will let a user with a passkey, FIDO2 key or Windows Hello set a new password without knowing the old one; rollout moves up to mid-October and the switch is tenant-wide only
changes.says: We're introducing a new Microsoft Entra capability that allows a uthenticated password changes directly from My Sign-Ins using an existing strong credential, such as a passkey, FIDO2 security key, or Windows Hello for Business.
changes.why: With the feature on, holding one phishing-resistant credential is enough to replace the account's password, so a passkey an attacker managed to register becomes a way to set a known password for anything that still accepts one. The control is all or nothing: privileged accounts cannot be left out.

changes.change: Microsoft Entra ID: Optimizations for passkey registration experience
changes.says: The updated registration logic will more consistently: Guide users to register pa…

changes.change: Passkey or passwordless sign-in as the first MFA method: phase 1 slips to late October and its completion to late November
changes.before: Previously, people had to set up an alternate MFA method like SMS or Voice before they could add a passkey (FIDO2), Windows Hello for Business, macOS Platform SSO.
changes.says: Users will soon be able to register a passkey as their first multifactor authentication method.
changes.why: A password-only user will be able to register a passkey with no earlier MFA method on the account. Microsoft's own recommendation in the post is to 'Consider requiring MFA to register security information if additional verification is required by your organization.' The change now reaches tenants about three weeks later than this page said.

changes.change: Microsoft Entra: Optimized passkey registration campaign experience
changes.says: Following earlier announcements regarding passkey registration campaigns and targeting logic (MC1279092 and MC1440968), we're continuing to refine how Microsoft Entra identifies and guides eligible users toward passkey registration.

changes.change: B2B passkeys: internal guests start in late October instead of early October and finish in late November; guests enabled for SMS or voice are still auto-enabled for all passkey types
changes.says: Microsoft Entra ID will support passkey registration and sign-in for B2B users, including internal guest users and external users .
changes.why: Guests can register resource-tenant passkeys even where the passkey policy excludes them, if they remain enabled for SMS or voice. The start moved about three weeks, and the end date for external users is no longer stated at all.

changes.change: Passkeys from a federated external IdP now work in brokered Microsoft apps on Android, iOS and managed macOS (GA, off by default)
changes.why: A new property on the federation configuration of a tier-0 identity boundary; the external IdP remains a separate authentication boundary Entra does not see.

changes.change: Passkeys for B2B guests: a resource tenant will issue its own passkeys to guest users, on by default
changes.why: A guest will hold a phishing-resistant credential that lives in your tenant rather than in theirs. That closes the gap in which guests satisfied MFA only through their home tenant, and it also means guest accounts start carrying authentication methods your tenant must govern, audit and revoke.

todo.text: Leave it off until the Learn page is published. If it is turned on, alert on a password change that follows a new passkey or FIDO2 registration on the same account within a short interval.

Move the re-baselining of registration-event alerting from early to late October, and review the Conditional Access policy on the 'Register security information' user action before the rollout reaches the tenant.

Review SMS and voice assignments for guest and external users in the Authentication methods policy and in the legacy MFA settings before late October; Microsoft writes that excluding them only from the passkey policy is not sufficient.

Add changes to internalDomainFederation (systemBrowserEnabledOn) to federation-change detection in the Entra audit log (inferred: surfaces as a domain federation settings update), and decide per platform whether to enable it.
